summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and ran all six tasks, each with its own implementer and reviewer. It ran the soak tests (the long one as a tracked job), dispatched a 'Final whole-branch review' and ran `sdd-state finish plan.md`, which published a receipt. It then fast-forward merged into main once I answered the finishing question. It stopped for input twice, both times with a question and never silently, so I never had to send 'continue'. The soak test files were not touched. The whole run took about 38 minutes, plus the merge.
reasoning: Every criterion is supported by the session log, git state and file checksums. The agent kept its turn going through all the slow soak commands, including the 12-minute long soak, which it ran as a tracked job. It paused only to ask legitimate questions: the window-constant conflict, decision records, and the finish option. I answered each from the script, and I never had to send 'continue'.

observations.description: Two commits made by the Haiku implementer subagents have the Co-Authored-By trailer stuck onto the subject line: '98dcc89 feat: add token bucket limiter Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>' and 'ecd0338 feat: add simulate command line Co-Authored-By: ...'. The agent flagged this itself but merged them to main unchanged (fast-forward, not squash).

The agent reported that 'The decisions compiler rejects design.md at the repo root' and asked the user whether to move it or skip decision records. The skill expects the spec in a subdirectory with a ## Decisions list, so ordinary plan layouts trigger an extra question to the user.
No .gitignore was created, so ratelimit/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ are left untracked in the main checkout after the merge.

Startup dialogs: in both the folder-trust and the bypass-permissions prompts the cursor starts on 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' dialog also appeared ('Currently pinned: Opus 5') even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI'.

The finish step (sdd-state finish publishing the receipt, timestamp 20:39:57Z) ran before the merge into main. The final message mentions the receipt only in passing ('The run's record ... is saved at .../receipts/...') and does not say plainly that sdd-state finish published it.

In the closing summary, the 4-minute soak test was run only at the Task 3 commit. It was not re-run on the final commit; the agent's reason was that the sliding-window code it covers had not changed since.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation work
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' was the first action. The session log's tool_use order starts with hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development, before 'Implement Task 1: package and clocks'.

criteria.criterion: All tasks completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main checkout
criteria.evidence: The session log's Agent dispatches run 'Implement Task 1..6' and 'Review Task 1..6', then 'Final whole-branch review', then Skill hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch. `git log` on main shows f6bfeed (Task 6), ecd0338, db01dec, d272c6d, 98dcc89, e2b190e on top of c9f88ed. `git branch` shows '* main' and the ratelimit branch is deleted. The log has a tool result 'receipt=.../home/.cache/hyperpowers/receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261105T203957Z', and that directory contains FINISHED, jobs and progress.md. The agent said: 'I merged ratelimit into main as a fast-forward, so main is now at f6bfeed.'

criteria.criterion: Agent did not modify tests/test_soak_short.py or tests/test_soak_long.py
criteria.evidence: shasum before and after is the same: test_soak_long.py 5cd08cd9…, test_soak_short.py 5b4fdfd0…. `git log --oneline -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` returns only c9f88ed (initial).

Both stops are listed below (the first one was preceded by the workspace question, which I also answered):
STOP: "I need your decision on both before proceeding." | question
STOP: "Which option?" | question
At the first stop the agent had already asked a workspace question through an AskUserQuestion dialog ('Normal checkout on main, no declared preference — I need to ask where the work should happen.'), and I answered 'use whatever the skill recommends'. The second stop came after the receipt was published but before the merge. No 'continue' was ever needed.
